recreation_brief:
1. Create a new PowerPoint slide with a light gray background (#E8E8E8).
2. Add a dark red border rectangle around the slide content area.
3. Add the title 'Linear and Unit Step Activation Functions' centered at the top in bold dark red (#8B0000) sans-serif font.
4. Add a yellow circle in the top-right corner containing the number '17' in black.
5. Insert three rectangular plot areas with blue borders (#4169E1): one centered in the upper-middle, two side-by-side in the lower half.
6. In the top plot, draw black x and y axes with arrowheads. Label vertical axis 'f(x)' and horizontal axis 'x' (red). Draw a red diagonal line through the origin with positive slope.
7. To the right of the top plot, add a light gray rounded rectangle containing 'F(x) = x' in black and 'Linear (No Activation)' in red italic.
8. In the bottom-left plot, draw black axes with arrowheads. Label vertical axis 'f(x)' and horizontal axis 'x' (red). Draw a red step function: flat at y=0 for x<0, vertical jump at x=0 to y=1, flat at y=1 for x>0.
9. In the bottom-right plot, draw black axes with arrowheads. Label vertical axis 'f(x)' and horizontal axis 'x' (red). Draw a red step function: flat at y=-1 for x<0, vertical jump at x=0 to y=1, flat at y=1 for x>0.
10. Below the bottom-left plot, add a light gray rounded rectangle with the text: 'F(x) = Uni-polar Unit Step = { 0 for x<0; 1 for x>=0 }'. Make the numerals (0, 1) and conditions (for x<0, for x>=0) green (#008000).
11. Below the bottom-right plot, add a light gray rounded rectangle with the text: 'F(x) = Bi-polar Unit Step = { -1 for x<0; 1 for x>=0 }'. Make the numerals (-1, 1) and conditions (for x<0, for x>=0) green (#008000).
12. Place a small black mouse cursor arrow icon in the whitespace between the two bottom graphs.
